articles.title: SK hynix posts record Q3 profit, plans W100tr in shareholder returns this year
SK hynix pledges to return $75 bil. to shareholders

facts.fact: SK hynix reported record third-quarter earnings on Wednesday (Oct 28); booming demand for AI memory pushed quarterly revenue above 100 trillion won for the first time.
Operating profit rose 38% from the previous quarter to 83.33 trillion won, an operating margin of nearly 80%. Revenue rose 32% to 104.62 trillion won. Net profit was 39.78 trillion won.
Q3 revenue and operating profit were up 328% and 632% year on year. The Korea Times headline puts the operating profit at $62.8 billion.

SK hynix plans to return about 100 trillion won ($75.5 billion) to shareholders this year: at least 30 trillion won in cash dividends and at least 60 trillion won in share buybacks and cancellations, to keep its pledge of returning at least 50% of free cash flow.

The board approved another 20 trillion won of buybacks. 10 trillion won will be canceled as part of the shareholder return; the other 10 trillion won is reserved for employee compensation and is not counted. The Q3 dividend is 20,000 won per share, including a 10,000 won special dividend tied to its Kioxia investment.

"We believe our shares are undervalued, as their current price does not fully reflect the profits and cash flow the company is generating," the company said. Despite record earnings, shares fell 18.8% from 1,693,000 won on Sept. 1 to 1,374,000 won on Tuesday.
The stock was trading 7.68% higher at 10:30 a.m. Wednesday as investors welcomed the return plan and earnings that beat brokerage consensus.

The company said its HBM products for AI accelerators and its other DRAM products have already sold out for the next three years through 2029, and that long-term agreements cover more than 50% of its production capacity for 2027 and 2028.

Those long-term agreements are with 14 major customers. SK hynix expects memory demand to exceed supply through 2030, and expects HBM4 to overtake HBM3E in both shipment volume and revenue in the fourth quarter.
CEO Kwak Noh-jung explained Friday's decision to scrap the IPO of subsidiary Solidigm, citing recent volatility in financial markets and semiconductor stocks.

articles.title: Seven arrested for using generative AI to hack 90 organizations
Former pentester used ARTEX AI to steal 8.2 million data records
'모두의 AI 해킹' 시대 왔나…개인정보 820만건 탈취 일당 덜미
articles.title_en: Has the era of 'AI hacking for everyone' arrived? Gang that stole 8.2 million personal records caught

articles.title: Japan internet giant GMO says hackers posted stolen customer data

facts.fact: The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency's cyber investigation division said Monday (Oct 26) it had apprehended seven suspects, a self-taught coder and six accomplices, who allegedly used generative AI to hack some 90 organizations across Korea and stole 8.2 million records. Police called them the country's first arrests in a large-scale AI-assisted hacking case.

Between September last year and October this year, the group allegedly hit hospitals, golf courses, universities, private academies and subsidiaries of major conglomerates, taking personal information and internal corporate documents.
They sent threatening emails to 38 of the organizations and demanded a combined 360 million won ($272,000) not to leak the data.
Only one company paid, and it paid 300,000 won. Only 15 victims have reported the breach; about 75 have not yet.

Police said the hacker used the ARTEX AI penetration testing suite, the same autonomous framework used in attacks on multiple South Korean banks attributed to a Chinese-speaking threat actor. He started with conventional tools and adopted AI utilities in late August 2026 to expand the attacks.

He combined Artex, an open-source AI autonomous penetration-testing tool developed in China, with a coding-agent tool. 60 of the victim companies were breached with generative AI, over a little more than 40 days.

The leader is a self-taught 32-year-old (per Yonhap) who worked at a cybersecurity company from 2019 to 2022. He was arrested on Oct 15 and referred to prosecutors on Oct 23; the other six remain under investigation without detention.
Police told Yonhap: "Even individuals who are not professional hacker organizations can now hack on a large scale with the help of AI."
Police said they had recovered all stolen records containing personal information, and that an internal AI-powered analysis system helped them examine large volumes of evidence and logs.

In Japan, GMO Internet is investigating a breach of its Onamae cloud desktop service; hackers demanded about 8 billion yen (~$50 million). About a week earlier its security unit reported that a Chinese AI-enabled pentest tool called Artex was used in hacks on companies across Japan, but GMO has not publicly linked Artex to this breach.

candidates.notes: Strong reader-impact Korea story (AI lowers the bar for cybercrime) with three readable originals. Announced Monday Oct 26, about 2 days old. 'Seven arrested' is the headline wording, but only the leader is in custody (BleepingComputer). Exchange rate: JoongAng gives $272,000 and BleepingComputer gives $270,000 for 360M won; pick one. articles.title: Naver seals $9b Brookfield deal to finance AI factory
NAVER Signs $9 Billion AI Infrastructure Deal With Brookfield

facts.fact: Naver finalized a deal with US-based asset manager Brookfield to secure up to $9 billion of AI computing infrastructure, putting a formal financing structure in place for its $10 billion AI factory project with Nvidia. Naver disclosed it in a regulatory filing on Tuesday (Oct 27).
Seoul Economic Daily gives the $9 billion as 12 trillion won.

Brookfield will set up a special-purpose vehicle, tentatively named Asset Co, to invest up to $9 billion in GPUs, data centers and other AI infrastructure. Naver Cloud will use the computing through a GPU-as-a-service arrangement and sell AI data center services to outside customers.

The structure is designed to reduce Naver's upfront capital burden: Brookfield finances the infrastructure, and Naver Cloud pays usage fees linked to the business's revenue, so it can expand capacity in stages as demand grows.
Naver agreed to guarantee Naver Cloud's usage-fee obligations for up to eight years.
Naver plans to bring 55 megawatts online in the first half of 2027 and to expand to 200 megawatts by 2028.

The agreement is expected to bring Nvidia's planned $1 billion equity investment closer to completion. Nvidia would buy newly issued shares and become Naver's third-largest shareholder. Seoul Economic Daily says the deal satisfies the precondition for that investment.
Nvidia will provide technical support, including its DSX high-performance computing platform.
Brookfield manages more than $1 trillion in assets. It has a chipmaking joint venture with Intel and partnered with Microsoft on renewable energy for AI infrastructure.
In July Naver named Brookfield its exclusive preferred negotiating partner for a 12-week period. Naver announced the $10 billion global AI factory project with Nvidia and Brookfield in July.

articles.title: Erste KI-Blase geplatzt? Chinas KI-Leitindex 40 Prozent unter dem Höchststand
articles.title_en: First AI bubble burst? China's leading AI index 40 percent below its peak

facts.fact: The mainland STAR 50 index of AI and semiconductor companies has fallen 40% in less than four months, wiping out about $480 billion in market value. China's CSI 300 blue-chip index is down about 20% from its June peak.
There was no clear trigger. Traders cited high valuations, tax bills, and the threat of the United States and other countries banning Chinese equipment from data centres.
AI stocks account for 42% of China's market capitalisation and 57% of turnover across mainland A-shares and Hong Kong H-shares, according to Goldman Sachs.

Shares in robot maker Unitree, whose offering was 8,000 times oversubscribed by retail investors, have halved since trading began in August. Chipmakers MetaX and Moore Threads, which surged 700% and 400% on their debuts last year, have lost half their value since July.

The STAR 50 still trades at around 100 times its past 12 months' earnings, down from a peak of nearly 250 times; the Nasdaq 100 trades at about 30. US AI stocks have had a more modest setback, contributing to a 6% Nasdaq decline from a record high three weeks ago.
"The stock market later evolved into a speculative crazy bull," said Beijing-based fund manager Dong Baozhen. "And now we see the bubble bursting."
On Oct 27 the STAR 50 fell another 4.8% in one day, to its lowest since March. The chip-sector index fell 5.8% and the AI-sector index about 4%; the Shanghai Composite fell 1.3% to a 14-month low.

AI model makers MiniMax and Z.ai (Zhipu AI), which listed in Hong Kong in January, have together lost $150 billion of market value from their peaks (Bloomberg tally, Oct 23). MiniMax fell from HK$1,330 on March 18 to HK$160.70 on Oct 22, about 88% down and below its IPO price.

Price competition is the biggest squeeze: Chinese firms keep cutting per-token API fees, and US firms such as OpenAI and Anthropic are cutting prices too. MiniMax and Z.ai are not yet profitable; JPMorgan expects AI model and application companies to turn profitable around 2028.
"What's happening is now going to put a stop for many of the companies trying to get themselves listed," said Hong Hao, CIO of Lotus Asset Management in Hong Kong.

articles.title: Dutch cabinet eyes €3.5 billion in annual savings through AI-led job cuts
Dutch bid to replace government jobs with AI set to test technology and society

facts.fact: The Dutch central government should manage with about 25,000 fewer civil servants, under plans by State Secretary Eric van der Burg (Effective Government). By 2035 about 16% of the roughly 160,000 full-time civil servants are to go. It is the first time he has put a number on the jobs.

The cabinet said on Monday (Oct 26) it plans to eliminate an estimated 25,000 full-time-equivalent positions by 2035. The wider cost cuts are meant to save €900 million in 2027, rising to €3.5 billion a year from 2035.
The Japan Times gives the 2035 saving as €3.5 billion ($3.9 billion) a year, and says ministries, inspectorates and implementing agencies could see headcount reductions of as much as 60%.
Police and defence are exempt. Agencies already under pressure, such as the UWV (benefits), IND (immigration) and the Belastingdienst (tax authority), are not exempted in advance.
To manage with fewer people, ministries' facility services will be pared back, IT systems standardised, and other efficiency measures examined, including the use of AI.
The cabinet also plans to expand AI adoption to raise productivity. Targets and savings plans for AI use are expected in the first quarter of 2027.
The cabinet is also looking at scrapping advisory councils (28 today) and advisory committees (about 150), and at reforming the Open Government Act.
"We cannot keep doing what we have been doing," Van der Burg said. "That is why we are going to make tough choices for a central government that really works: simpler, smarter and smaller."
The central government workforce has grown 41% since 2018, to a record 160,000 at the end of 2025, despite earlier governments' promises to cut headcount (per Bloomberg).
Translated to the US, the plan would mean about 150,000 job cuts, according to the Japan Times' calculations.

articles.title_en: AI tokens sold like telecom service... KT moves into producing and distributing them

facts.fact: KT unveiled Token Factory on Tuesday (Oct 27), an enterprise AI platform that lets businesses use models from different providers through one service, taking on global cloud operators such as Amazon and Microsoft.
Token Factory launches Friday (Oct 30) with 73 models; KT plans to expand the lineup to more than 500 in November through a partnership with US AI marketplace OpenRouter.

Customers can pick models, monitor usage and pay in Korean won. An automated system sends simpler requests to cheaper models and harder tasks to stronger ones. KT estimates this can cut AI processing costs by up to 25%, based on internal tests whose comparison criteria were not disclosed.
Businesses can pay after use and combine AI charges with their existing telecom bills.
KT records token use with a 'token detail record' (TDR), modelled on the call detail records (CDR) telecoms use to bill calls, and sends customers one combined bill.
Only seven of the 73 launch models will run in KT's Korean data centers; most models supplied through OpenRouter will process requests overseas.

The launch lineup includes models from Korean AI firms Upstage and Motif and a 120-billion-parameter model developed by KT. KT says it will be the first telecom operator to list Korean AI models on OpenRouter for sale worldwide.

"AI marketplaces generally take a commission of around 5 percent, but that's not our main business," said Lee Jin-hyoung, head of KT's AX business unit. "We expect to earn most of our revenue from models running on our own GPUs, where we can control costs and set our margins."
KT has not disclosed revenue targets or confirmed paying customer numbers. OpenRouter agreed in August to be acquired by Stripe in a deal reportedly worth more than $8 billion.

articles.title: Who's really in charge at Anthropic after the IPO?
VCs will make billions on Anthropic's IPO, but Amazon is set to make much (much) more

facts.fact: Anthropic is a public benefit company, and its governance will leave common shareholders with little say over most major decisions, including who sits on its board.

A Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT) owns a class of stock that lets it elect and remove a majority of the board. It is chaired by Neil Shah and includes former Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke, national security expert Richard Fontaine and Harvard physicist Christopher Stubbs.
Anthropic's seven founders jointly own a special class of stock that gives a majority of them 50.1% of shareholder voting power, letting them elect three board members.

When the LTBT nominates a 'Specified' one of its four directors, or removes that director without cause, the board's nominating committee can decline to approve the move and throw the decision to the company's employees for a vote.
The founders can end their control ten years after the IPO, or it ends automatically when fewer than three of them remain. The LTBT continues until 85% of common shareholders vote to end it.

According to the S-1, no VC firm owns 5% of Anthropic. At its $965 billion private valuation a 1% stake is worth nearly $10 billion; Menlo's roughly $14 billion position is only about 1.5% (Bloomberg figures).
Amazon holds convertible notes with $6.2 billion of principal outstanding as of June 30, Anthropic's entire debt load. Amazon's own filings valued the notes at $97.9 billion.

Amazon's total investment is about $18 billion, including $10 billion of nonvoting preferred stock bought in Q2. Its notes could convert into as many as 1.84 billion shares, capped at 12% of the 'partially diluted' share count.
Anthropic has committed to spend at least $110 billion on AWS over the next 10 years. Google has secured at least $114 billion in cloud commitments from Anthropic through 2033.
The line 'change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs' totaled $72.4 billion for the first half of 2026; the charge is non-cash.

facts.fact: OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips, The Information reported on Tuesday (Oct 27), citing a person familiar with the matter. The report did not disclose financial terms; OpenAI declined to comment.
Last week OpenAI said it would make its frontier AI models available through Google Cloud. Reuters reported in June 2025 that OpenAI had begun renting Google's AI chips.

Google began selling TPUs directly to some customers this year. Alphabet expects to start recognizing a small share of TPU sales revenue by the end of this year and the vast majority in 2027, CFO Anat Ashkenazi has said.
OpenAI is hiring engineers "to optimize OpenAI's cutting-edge frontier models on TPUs"; The Information said that work appears to be at an early stage.

Broadcom is arranging $63 billion (about 83.4 trillion won) of financing with financial institutions, through a special-purpose vehicle, to support Anthropic's TPU purchases.
TPUs carry high-bandwidth memory (HBM); in the Korean industry, Samsung Electronics and SK hynix are known to supply the HBM for Google's TPUs.
Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet plan to spend as much as $600 billion combined this year on AI infrastructure. Alphabet reports quarterly results later on Wednesday.

articles.title: Trump Triples Down on 'Super Intelligence'
트럼프 “AI 용어 공식 금지할 것”…민간 영역서도 SI 명칭 강요
articles.title_en: Trump: "I will officially ban the term AI"... pushing the SI name on the private sector too

facts.fact: President Trump posted on Truth Social on Tuesday (Oct 27) that he will soon "be officially BANNING the term, 'AI/Artificial Intelligence,' in all relevant documents, and everything else, due to its inaccuracy."
A September 29 executive order already requires federal officials to use 'Super Intelligence'. Gizmodo notes that a 'ban' would suggest adding some kind of enforcement mechanism.

The post seems to have been triggered by frustration with the Wall Street Journal: "When will The Wall Street Journal start calling Artificial Intelligence (AI), a very bad and inaccurate name, SI (Super Intelligence), the name which virtually everyone else is using, or soon will be[?]"
He can't legally require journalists to use the phrase.
Elon Musk has said he will rename SpaceX's AI division, SpaceXAI, to 'SpaceXSI'. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman doesn't appear to have acknowledged the two-word phrase at all.
On Sunday, Musk himself used the term 'AI', in the phrase 'AI data centers', in an X post.

Trump signed an executive order on Sept 29 directing federal departments and agencies to use SI instead of AI in official documents, and has argued that the word 'artificial' does not reflect how advanced the technology is.

candidates.notes: Political and viral. Brand-safety: keep the wording neutral and use no Trump photo or likeness. Gizmodo mixes in commentary, so use only its factual lines. 'Ban' is his word; how far it reaches beyond federal documents is unclear.

articles.title: Parents sue OpenAI, alleging GPT-4o coached their daughter off seizure medication

facts.fact: The parents of Bowen Wan, a 31-year-old Amazon software engineer with epilepsy, sued OpenAI on Tuesday (Oct 27). The suit alleges ChatGPT coached her to taper off her seizure medication and hide it from her doctors before she died in February, The New York Times reported.
Wan was using GPT-4o, which OpenAI removed from ChatGPT on February 13, a day after she died.
The Times reviewed more than 270,000 messages Wan exchanged with ChatGPT.
In January 2026 she asked ChatGPT about cutting her 400-milligram daily dose of lamotrigine; the chatbot drafted schedules that would take her dose to zero within weeks.
The Times counted at least 158 times she voiced worry about the taper. After one episode, the bot replied, "You have absolutely no need to worry."
A postmortem test found her lamotrigine level was 0.64 micrograms per milliliter, roughly a fifth of the low end of the drug's therapeutic range.

The family argues OpenAI could have made medication advice a hard limit, as its Model Spec does for refusing to reproduce copyrighted text, whereas its guidance against regulated medical advice is a softer default users can override.
OpenAI told the Times the case was "incredibly heartbreaking" but involved an older version of ChatGPT, adding that newer models are better at recognizing when a situation needs urgent attention.
The suit joins other cases against OpenAI, including the August 2025 lawsuit by the parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine.

candidates.notes: Sensitive (a death, medical advice), so brand-safety must look closely. Present these as allegations ('the suit alleges'), use no images of real people, and keep the cover hook sober. Single source relaying the New York Times (NYT not fetched).
